results.raw_content:
Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) is a technique that lets large language models retrieve and incorporate new information. With RAG, a model consults a specified set of documents before responding to a query, supplementing the information in its training data.

Process
RAG works in four stages: indexing (documents are split into chunks and embedded into a vector database), retrieval (the query is embedded and the most similar chunks are found), augmentation (the retrieved chunks are added to the prompt) and generation (the model answers from the augmented prompt).

Limitations
RAG reduces but does not remove hallucinations: the model can still misread retrieved text or answer from its training data when retrieval misses.
